text:
autoscaler-bot: ALERT: gpu-pool-usw1 capacity exhausted in cluster-redwood-prod (90% rejected requests)

maria: seeing 503s from hosted-api in us-west1, looks like GPU queue is jammed :grimacing:

lee: confirmed - cluster autoscaler tried to scale but API responded with QUOTA_EXCEEDED on node creation. GCP quota shows GPUs at 100/100.

raj: who launched the big batch in prod? any runaway jobs?

katie: i just spotted a training job from 'research-team' namespace that requested 32 gpus with no limits. Pod name: research-batch-2026-03-18-9. It's Pending and creating pods in parallel.

maria: ok, priority: stop the runaway pod, free GPUs, and fall back traffic to dedicated pool if possible. raj can you cordon the nodepool?

raj: on it. cordoning nodePool gpu-pool-usw1. command: `gcloud container clusters resize cluster-redwood-prod --node-pool=gpu-pool-usw1 --num-nodes=0 --zone=us-west1-b` (not executing until we confirm)

lee: hold on, resizing to 0 will evict legit serving instances. Better action: kubectl delete pod research-batch-2026-03-18-9 -n research-team --grace-period=0 --force

katie: killing now. `kubectl -n research-team delete pod research-batch-2026-03-18-9 --grace-period=0 --force`

autoscaler-bot: ACTION: Pod research-batch-2026-03-18-9 deleted at 1710634218 by katie

maria: good. we need immediate mitigation to restore serving capacity: can we temporarily increase autoscaler max and request emergency quota from GCP?

lee: increased cluster-autoscaler max nodes for gpu-pool-usw1 from 50 to 80 (patch applied). Setting emergency label to avoid autoscaler backoff.

devops-bot: NOTE: quota request to GCP submitted (case 12345678) — response SLA 1-2 hours.

raj: routing traffic to dedicated-gpu-pool in us-west1 now. Updating service routing: `kubectl patch svc hosted-api -n platform -p '{"spec":{"externalTrafficPolicy":"Local"}}'` then update config to prefer dedicated-gpu-pool.

maria: also apply a temporary namespace-level ResourceQuota to research-team to prevent >8 GPUs per namespace.

katie: applied: `kubectl apply -f - <<EOF
apiVersion: v1
kind: ResourceQuota
metadata:
  name: rq-gpu-temp
  namespace: research-team
spec:
  hard:
    limits.nvidia.com/gpu: "8"
EOF`

lee: checking cluster health/metrics. current GPU utilization: gpu-pool-usw1 nodes=50 (all full), queue latency 1200ms, pod pending=23, failed node creations=7.

maria: summarize quick action list for postmortem. we need to fix autoscaler backoff behavior and add quota guardrails.

raj: quick list: 1) enforce namespace GPU limits via admission controller 2) mark high-cost namespaces with billing alerts 3) autoscaler: disable exponential backoff on quota errors 4) provide safer default for batch job templates 5) add emergency redirect runbook

katie: cost note: if we scale to 80 nodes and they stay up for 2h that's ~ (30 GPUs/node * 30? wait) — rough calc: estimated $Xk, will add proper calc in ticket.

maria: opened incident ticket INF-2026-033 and assigned to eng-infra and SRE for follow-up. Link: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/INF-2026-033

sre-oncall: leaving this thread once all pending pods drop below 5 and external errors <1%. monitoring alert thresholds reduced until postmortem done.

lee: final check: pending pods now 0, rejection rate back to 0.5%. restoring normal routing, scaling gpu-pool-usw1 down to 50 nodes slowly to avoid churn.

maria: thanks everyone. postmortem owners: raj+lee+katie. we'll schedule RCA and changes in infra sprint. :thumbsup:
